clue.text: Shed light on playwright cutting opening act after sacking name

indicators.note: to cut an opening is to chop off the first letter of the word in front
sacking means dismissing, so the abbreviation for name is thrown out of the word

parts.note: Harold Pinter, the playwright
to act is to pretend
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone explains how a playwright trimmed a first act after firing a big name from the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutting opening act' reads as one phrase about trimming a show; actually 'cutting opening' works on the playwright and 'act' starts a new piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to explain it, so a thing interpreted has had light shed on it.

clue.text: Intelligence agent finally abandoning them?

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter is dropped from what follows

parts.note: them are, playfully, the people who are not us

indicators.note: 'finally' keeps only the last letter of 'agent'

parts.note: the last letter of agent

explanation.surface: A spy who has finally deserted asks whether the intelligence service is now his enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading of them as NOT US; take out T and the rest closes up.
explanation.definitionFit: Nous is a British informal word for common sense or practical cleverness.

clue.text: A head teacher is more than enough

indicators.note: the word teacher has more letters than are needed, so the wanted ones sit inside it with spares around them

parts.note: the inner letters of teacher

explanation.surface: One head teacher is plenty for any school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A head teacher' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'A head', as in 'five pounds a head'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying a price is so much a head means it is charged per person, which is each.

clue.text: First-class officers drop at speed

parts.note: a plum job or role is a first-class one
the Met, London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Top-ranking officers fall from favour very quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: To plummet is to fall steeply and fast, a verb for a rapid drop.

clue.text: Index promoting the latest amphibians found locally

indicators.note: promoting the latest means moving the final letter up to the front of the word

parts.note: the FTSE 100 is the London stock market index

explanation.surface: A share index favours whatever amphibians are newest in the area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found locally' marks a dialect word: eft is a regional and old name for a newt.
explanation.definitionFit: Efts are newts in dialect, small amphibians known by that name in parts of Britain.

clue.text: Say scripture over epitaph for personal boost

parts.note: e.g., for example, is another way to say 'say'
the Old Testament
Rest In Peace, the classic gravestone epitaph

explanation.surface: Reading out scripture over a grave as a way to feel good about yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity done chiefly to flatter oneself, a boost to one's own self-image.

clue.text: Republic once keen to corral extremely Stalinist crowds

indicators.note: to corral is to pen livestock in, so one word encloses another

parts.note: keen means eager

indicators.note: extremely points to the two extremes, the very first and last letters

parts.note: the outside letters of Stalinist
crowds, as a noun, are the many

explanation.surface: A former republic was eager to herd the masses in a thoroughly Stalinist way.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stalinist surface fits the answer, a Soviet-bloc state, which makes the definition easy to spot once the split is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: The German Democratic Republic was the communist state that existed until reunification in 1990.

clue.text: Option for garden door kept her busy

indicators.note: busy suggests bustling activity, so the letters are all moved about

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a garden feature says looking after the door kept her occupied.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-hot poker is a tall flowering plant, Kniphofia, a popular choice for a garden border.

clue.text: Boat race without gold, for one

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the word for gold is taken out

parts.note: taken as written
or is gold in heraldry
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: A boat race where nobody wins a gold medal, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boat race' is Cockney rhyming slang, and the comma splits 'for one' away from 'gold'; or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang boat race stands for face, the word it rhymes with.

clue.text: United Kingdom perhaps deposing leader seen with pre-Euro currency, over 100 marks

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the currency is laid over and around the number

parts.note: the punt was Ireland's currency before the euro
C is the Roman numeral for 100

indicators.note: deposing a leader removes the one at the head, so the first letter goes

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United
a kingdom is one example of a nation

explanation.surface: The United Kingdom loses its leader as the old currency gains more than a hundred marks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United Kingdom' must be split: United and 'Kingdom perhaps' are separate pieces, and only the second loses its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Punctuation is the set of marks, such as commas and full stops, used in writing.

clue.text: Long delay in Bow

indicators.note: Bow is in London's East End, where Cockney speech drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a hitch is a delay or snag

explanation.surface: A long holdup in an East London district.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is the Cockney heartland, and Cockneys are said to drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: To itch for something is to long for it, a verb of restless desire.

clue.text: I identified hiding spots to northern lawmaker

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something hiding another keeps it tucked away inside

parts.note: to identify something is to see it, past tense saw
acne is an outbreak of spots
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: Someone reports spotting pimples on a lawmaker from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lawmaker' suggests a legislator; here it is the scientist behind the laws of motion and gravitation.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton formulated the laws of motion, so he is a lawmaker in the scientific sense.

clue.text: Drug taken by Clare, partly for sport

parts.note: a tablet is a pill
Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland, so part of Clare

explanation.surface: A woman named Clare takes some medicine to help her play sport.
explanation.walkthrough: Clare looks like a woman's name, but it is the Irish county whose main town is Ennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, or ping-pong, is a sport played with bats and a light ball across a net on a table.

clue.text: Found lying around in France, the next Brigitte Bardot?

indicators.note: lying around something means sprawled about it, so one word surrounds the other

parts.note: to found something is to start it
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A girl discovered lounging about in France could become the next Brigitte Bardot.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma tempts a stop after France, but 'the' belongs to the wordplay as the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: A starlet is a young actress tipped for fame, as Bardot once was.

clue.text: One who monologued for A Bennett's degree class

parts.words: One who monologued for A Bennett
parts.note: Thora Hird starred in Alan Bennett's Talking Heads monologues

explanation.surface: An actor in Alan Bennett's monologues reveals what class of degree the writer earned.
explanation.walkthrough: The actress is reduced to initial and surname, T. Hird. Talking Heads is Bennett's series of TV monologues.
explanation.definitionFit: A third is the lowest class of honours degree awarded at British universities.

clue.text: Colouring agents from USA filling hole

indicators.note: a filling goes inside something, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a pit is a hole in the ground
G-men are FBI agents in American slang

explanation.surface: Paint agents from America fill a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colouring agents' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at Colouring.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigment is a substance that gives colour, a colouring.

clue.text: One of 150 seats, after landslide, initially claimed by Starmer?

indicators.note: something claimed by another is taken into its hold, so it goes inside

parts.note: Keir Starmer became Prime Minister in 2024

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: the opening letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A party leader takes a huge number of seats after an election landslide.
explanation.walkthrough: The 2024 landslide gave Labour over 400 seats; the 150 is the number of psalms in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Psalms contains 150 sacred songs, so a psalm is one of 150.

clue.text: I play the odds

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; this is what one would say

parts.note: taken as written
SP is the starting price, the odds on a horse at the off

explanation.surface: A gambler boasts of betting on the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I play' sounds like a gambler, but it is what an actor might say of a role.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesp, short for thespian, is an actor, someone who plays parts on stage.

clue.text: Fire consuming middle of rolling pin

indicators.note: consuming means swallowing up, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to fire an employee is to axe them

indicators.note: the middle of a word is the letter at its very centre

parts.note: the central letter of rolling

explanation.surface: A fire burns up the middle of a rolling pin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling pin' is a kitchen tool, but the definition is pin alone.
explanation.definitionFit: An axle is the rod or spindle on which a wheel turns, a pin in the mechanical sense.

clue.text: Rounds of skinless meat

indicators.note: with its skin removed, the outer layer, the first and last letters, is stripped off

parts.note: gammon is cured ham

explanation.surface: Several servings of meat with the skin taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammo is short for ammunition, counted in rounds fired from a gun.

clue.text: Turn after junction, seeing bridge obstruction?

parts.note: a T-junction
to roll is to turn over

explanation.surface: A driver turns after a junction and finds a bridge blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places ROLL behind T. The question mark is for the fairy-tale troll who guards a bridge, as in Three Billy Goats Gruff.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore a troll lurks under a bridge and blocks travellers from crossing.

clue.text: Dog sitting outside former royal houses

indicators.note: sitting outside something means being wrapped around it

parts.note: to dog someone is to track or trace them
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A dog sits outside the homes of a one-time royal.
explanation.walkthrough: Dog looks like the animal but is a verb, meaning to follow someone's trail.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a row of houses joined together, very common in British streets.

clue.text: Unsophisticated curry served up on plate

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means sent upwards, so the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: dal is a lentil curry
a dish is a plate

explanation.surface: A crude curry is dished up on a plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Laddish behaviour is boisterous and crude, typical of young men, so lacking refinement.

clue.text: Warm saw?

definitions.meaning: first meaning, split in two: something warm

explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as NOT ICED for the first meaning; read whole it means saw.
explanation.definitionFit: To have noticed something is to have seen it, and a drink not iced is warm.

clue.text: Show me grasping a point

indicators.note: grasping means holding tight, so one piece is gripped inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
a tine is a prong or point

explanation.surface: A request to demonstrate how to hold a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is an afternoon performance of a play or film, a type of show.

clue.text: Due to drop round camp

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so that letter is removed

parts.note: money due is owing
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone is expected to drop by the camp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drop round' reads as visit; here drop is the deletion and round is the letter shaped like a circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is a faction within a party or movement, as is a camp.

clue.text: Item computers etc screened, displaying over and over again?

definitions.text: Item computers etc screened, displaying over and over again?

indicators.note: over means turned back, and over again means the turned piece is repeated
screened here means kept out of view, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
IT, information technology

explanation.surface: A thing seen on computer screens that keeps appearing again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: ITEM without IT leaves EM, turned over to ME and then repeated. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is an image or idea shared and reposted across the internet over and over.

clue.text: Peak time for journey's end, about noon

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: estimated time of arrival
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: Reaching the summit at the end of the trip at around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the volcanic mountain in Sicily, a peak.

clue.text: G.I. departed

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An American soldier has left.
explanation.walkthrough: G.I. looks like the US soldier; read letter by letter it is G and the numeral I.
explanation.definitionFit: Gone and departed both mean having left, or euphemistically having died.

clue.text: I mostly love an eccentric closing act's send-off

indicators.note: closing means shutting in, so the jumbled letters close around the next piece
eccentric means odd and off-centre, so the letters are scattered into a new order
mostly means not all, so the last letter of the word is lost

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, then cut short
taken as written
an act of parliament is a decree, an edict

explanation.surface: A farewell speech at the end of a show, featuring an odd declaration of love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Closing act' reads as a final performance; here closing is the container signal and act is EDICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A valediction is a farewell, a speech or words said as a send-off.

clue.text: Overlook first from Oxford University

indicators.note: first from means take only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the opening letter of Oxford
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

explanation.surface: Someone forgets which comes first, Oxford or a university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oxford University' reads as one name; University alone is MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, to overlook it.

clue.text: Plane directed down to earth

parts.note: plane as an adjective means flat, level
headed means steered in a direction

explanation.surface: An aircraft is steered down to the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Plane suggests an aircraft and 'down to earth' a landing; plane means flat here.
explanation.definitionFit: A level-headed person is sensible and practical, which is what down-to-earth means.
